title: AI-Driven Job Application Engine
summary: Engineered an AI-driven automation tool using LLM-based code generation to streamline job application workflows; integrated multi-provider LLM failover across Cerebras, Groq, OpenRouter, and DeepSeek.

flow.detail: Cerebras · Groq · OpenRouter · DeepSeek, with cooldown + failover

problem: Job hunting is repetitive: finding roles, tailoring a CV, and retyping the same answers into long, inconsistent application forms. Free-tier LLMs can do the thinking, but they rate-limit and disappear without warning.
built: An LLM router that spreads work across free-tier providers. A 429 puts a provider on cooldown until its limit resets, and a model that is refused is benched on its own instead of taking its whole provider down.
An application filler that walks multi-page forms, including Workday, up to the final Submit, then hands off to me.
Safety guards: every write is verified and scoped to the page and document it belongs to, with answer provenance, so it never guesses at a field or claims something untrue.
A phone-friendly dashboard with a Today view, push notifications when a form is ready or a reply arrives, and remote access to the app’s browser.
result: In active use for my own job search. Roughly 160 commits over two weeks, built with AI-assisted development (Claude Code).
note: Private repository: I’m happy to walk through the code or a live demo on request. It builds on the open-source Career-Ops project (MIT); the LLM router, application filler, safety guards and phone dashboard are my work.
